title: In-flight session sync can restore a connected snapshot after disconnect
reasoning: syncBrowserSession only invalidates older syncs when another sync starts, then applies a connected snapshot after both status and get_tabs complete. disconnectBrowserSession closes the browser and applies a disconnected snapshot, but it does not invalidate any already-running sync request. If a poll sync started just before disconnect and finishes afterward with stale connected data, it can apply lines 227-237 and put the UI back into a connected state even though close already succeeded.
reproduction: Have a connected session with polling active. Let syncBrowserSession start and complete the status request, then trigger disconnectBrowserSession before get_tabs resolves. If get_tabs resolves with the pre-close tab list after disconnect applies its disconnected snapshot, the older sync can reapply connected=true.
recommendation: Invalidate pending syncs before state-changing actions such as disconnect, for example by incrementing syncRequestId at the start of disconnectBrowserSession or by using a dedicated generation token shared by sync and mutations. After close succeeds, ignore any sync result that began before the disconnect generation.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for this feature, and the package test script only shows a general Jest entrypoint without evidence of race coverage for this store.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Jest test that stubs IpcBridge.invoke so a status/get_tabs sync is paused, calls disconnectBrowserSession while it is in flight, then resolves the stale get_tabs call and asserts getBrowserSessionSnapshot().connected remains false.
minimumFixScope: frontend/src/renderer/infrastructure/runtime/browserSessionStore.js plus a focused renderer store test.
